mandatory_tasks.surface: six real customer projects / bounded Lilies-first attempt / fresh isolated Codex public-API fallback Builder / observable rerun telemetry / causal supplementation ledger / independent denominators / generic capability lane
mandatory_tasks.acceptance: A bounded Lilies-first attempt with the decoupled sibling ../LiliesAgent is retained with builder_actor=lilies, its exact measured token usage and eight-phase timing, and its terminal failure; that failed attempt does not satisfy any project. EXP-LILIES-001 through EXP-LILIES-006 then run one by one with a fresh isolated Codex fallback Builder context for every final-eligible project attempt. Each final attempt starts with a fresh empty application, fresh customer-environment generation, fresh BuildAssignment, fresh session and task-scoped credential; customer environments run sequentially and stop after evidence capture. The final Builder receives an explicit allowlist containing only the public requirement package, block manual, public schemas, general public Builder guidance and task-scoped public platform contract and APIs, and it creates, incrementally edits, tests, runs, inspects public traces and artifacts, and publishes only through those APIs. It cannot read platform or LiliesAgent source, Git metadata, platform databases, developer workspaces, protected inputs, hidden seeds, expected state, oracle data or expected-versus-actual verifier differences, and the harness cannot prebuild or directly edit the workflow or reveal protected results. Any context exposed to source, protected content, oracle data or verifier differences is permanently ineligible as a final Builder and may act only as a separately authorized developer or coordinator; this includes the current root coordination context after its protected-content exposure incident. The already-published reused-application EXP-LILIES-001 version predates that incident but remains an intermediate harness and workflow result with fresh_empty=false and eligible_for_final=false, so it cannot satisfy final public-debug or protected-seed acceptance. Every attempt records builder_actor as lilies or codex_fallback, the exact context, assignment, session and application identities, public-material allowlist digest and exposure eligibility, while preserving every historical Lilies and Codex attempt, revision, actor, failure and evidence. Each Lilies Builder assignment or session has max_session_tokens=1000000; exceeding the recorded limit or issuing another model request after it fails the attempt. Codex token usage is recorded exactly when an authoritative counter is exposed; otherwise it is recorded as unknown or unavailable and is never estimated or represented as zero. The durable observable record contains public session messages or concise actions, public tool calls and results, explicit errors, workflow mutations, tests, runs, traces, artifacts, host receipts, publication results and timestamps, but never private chain-of-thought. Every elapsed interval belongs exactly once to environment/bootstrap, daemon discovery, explicit pairing, assignment/provision, Builder execution, host-result verification, platform/archive verification, or cleanup/reporting; actor-inapplicable discovery or pairing phases are recorded as zero-duration not_applicable, and phase start, end, duration and percentage sum to 100 percent within rounding. After publication, a task-author-controlled independent verifier runs one public debug case and three protected seed cases against the same immutable published version without repair between them; any failure requires a new retained final attempt from a fresh empty application and environment. Protected inputs, oracle content and expected-versus-actual differences never enter Builder or developer-visible records. The portfolio retains separate immutable denominators and covers supplier-document reconciliation on Paperless and InvenTree, access-controlled cited RAG on BookStack, durable event automation on Home Assistant, versioned ML or DL maintenance triage on ThingsBoard, structured finance artifact delivery on Actual, and forecast-driven constrained replenishment on ERPNext. EXP-LILIES-006 remains the mandatory primary ML-training denominator and must perform chronological split, fit or train, evaluation and backtest, immutable model version, promotion or deployment, inference and a retraining trigger; import-only or forecast-only evidence cannot satisfy it. Each non-technical project report explains task and seed design, business and natural-language workflow logic, intermediate and final outputs, failures and public repair path, tokens and phase shares, capabilities added, unresolved software or model gaps and environment limits. A platform supplement is allowed only after public evidence proves a reusable capability gap; the Builder role ends before supplementation, a separately authorized developer makes the minimal generic change, and a fresh isolated Builder reruns the affected project from a fresh application and environment. The supplement must contain no host-specific endpoint, field, mapping, adapter, wrapper, hidden answer or final graph, pass a non-source generality check, and remain linked as Builder gap report, developer supplementation and verification, and affected-project rerun or reprobe. T01H passes only when all six r8 Codex-fallback final attempts independently pass their public debug case and all three protected seeds with every failed and intermediate attempt retained. Portfolio averages, mock substitution, capability tests, another project evidence, prior Codex or Lilies success, the current reused application, or direct host manipulation cannot mask a failure. Only then may execution continue in the fixed order T01M, T01N, T01I and T01J.
mandatory_tasks.required_evidence: The locked r8 portfolio and per-project manifests; the bounded Lilies-first failure with builder_actor=lilies, exact authoritative token usage, the 1,000,000-token configuration, terminal status and complete eight-phase spans; an incident record marking the current root coordination context protected-content-exposed and ineligible for final Builder or verifier use without reproducing protected content; the already-published reused-application EXP-LILIES-001 result marked intermediate=true, fresh_empty=false and eligible_for_final=false; and, for every final project attempt, a fresh empty application, customer-environment generation, BuildAssignment, session, task-scoped credential and fresh isolated Codex context with builder_actor=codex_fallback. Required final evidence also includes the explicit public-file and public-API allowlist and digest, deny-by-default workspace and forbidden-assistance scans proving no platform or LiliesAgent source, Git, database, developer workspace, protected input, hidden seed, oracle or expected-versus-actual access; complete public platform API, action, error, mutation, test, run, trace, artifact, host-receipt and publication records with timestamps but no private reasoning; exact Codex token counters when authoritative counters exist and explicit unknown or unavailable values otherwise, never estimates or false zeroes; non-overlapping environment/bootstrap, daemon-discovery, pairing, assignment/provision, Builder-execution, host-verification, platform/archive-verification and cleanup/reporting spans, including zero-duration not_applicable actor phases, with starts, ends, durations and percentages summing to 100 percent within rounding; every frozen package revision, environment, public source and interface digest, budget, draft, test, run, trace, artifact, host receipt, publication, archive, model provider and cost; one public-debug result and three independently executed protected-seed results against the same immutable published version with no repair between cases and protected contents withheld from Builder and developer contexts; complete per-project attempt denominators and non-technical reports covering task and seed design, natural-language business and workflow logic, intermediate and final outputs, failure-to-repair path, token use and phase-time shares; preservation links for all historical Lilies and Codex attempts and failures; a fresh independent closure reviewer that has not seen protected content; and, for every supplementation cycle, the immutable Builder-gap, generic-developer-supplementation and affected-project fresh-rerun triplet with exact report revision, capability provenance, project revision, attempt and digest links, non-source generality verification and bounded history replay.

mandatory_tasks.surface: standalone sibling repository / daemon and CLI / macOS desktop / safe discovery / token observability
mandatory_tasks.acceptance: The decoupled Lilies implementation lives in the sibling ../LiliesAgent repository under the agent directory with its own Python distribution, Git history, daemon and CLI, private state, tests and native macOS SwiftPM application. It runs without importing agent_platform or sharing the platform database or tokens. The platform locates only a same-user, mode-0600, non-symlink discovery record, verifies a loopback public health fingerprint, and requires an explicit one-time pairing code; discovery never grants authority and the platform never reads the daemon bootstrap secret. Provider egress remains disabled by default, no startup or idle workflow consumes model tokens, and persisted usage is reportable by session, stage and model with unknown usage labeled rather than estimated. The desktop application can create, attach, resume and stop sessions, display messages, permissions and token usage, and survive daemon restart.
mandatory_tasks.required_evidence: Sibling-repository boundary and import scans; package, Python, CLI, daemon-restart and Swift tests; secure file-mode, owner, no-follow, fingerprint, bootstrap and pairing negative tests; real separate-process platform bridge and event replay; default-egress and idle no-token audit; per-stage and per-model usage fixtures; macOS build, launch and visual inspection; sanitized manifests and independent read-only security review.

mandatory_tasks.surface: standalone DevelopmentAssignment broker / autonomous agent collaboration / scoped software tools
mandatory_tasks.acceptance: The standalone Lilies project can execute an explicitly created DevelopmentAssignment against an arbitrary authorized software workspace through a model-and-tool loop with frozen role, path, command, network, side-effect, deadline and budget grants. Unattended autonomous handoff removes per-message human supervision but never lets an executor mint, resolve or widen its own authority. File and process tools are bounded, cancellable and isolated; complete process groups are reaped; every side effect has a durable prepared record before execution, restart-ambiguous effects require reconciliation instead of blind replay, and stable idempotency prevents duplicate mutations. Model calls use the same persisted stage and model token ledger and remain impossible while provider egress is disabled.
mandatory_tasks.required_evidence: Strict assignment and grant schemas; resolver and executor separation with self-approval denial; workspace escape, state-directory, symlink, command, network, output, cancellation and descendant-process negative tests; prepared, running, settled and reconciliation restart tests; stable-idempotency and duplicate-effect tests; independent-process API and CLI transcript; deterministic-provider end-to-end development fixture with complete tool, diff, test and usage evidence; independent security review.

mandatory_tasks.surface: separate Android software project / Lilies developer assignment / emulator or device

Direct Codex implementation, a generated skeleton, static source inspection or another project's evidence cannot count as completion; the result is a software-development pressure test with enterprise_denominator=false.
mandatory_tasks.required_evidence: Frozen project brief and baseline digest; isolated Lilies session, assignment and grant; complete model, token and tool transcript; per-iteration commits, diffs and tests; pinned Android toolchain and reproducible build command; APK or bundle digest; emulator or device screenshots, logs and acceptance results; security scan and independent review.
